rows.act: TWO OF FOUR DRAINED INSIDE THE FIRST HOUR. TO-CG-G-1 (the census) @15bfeb3a62 and TO-CG-G-3 (the substrate card) @91654ab3c6, both instances VALID rc 0 verified IN THEIR WORKTREES before the merge; slot ~2 closed; no org/modules/graph path in either merge, so no comp-system pass owed. THE CENSUS ANSWERED THE BINDING CONDITION AND NARROWED THE SEAM: 29 of 59 node classes carry two identity strings, but only 15 nodes of 27,665 are KEYED BY the second, and all 15 are the whole of S3_BUCKET_POLICY -- the only place in the estate where an edge built on a resource's other name finds a real node, which is why 135 wrong-class landings read as resolutions. 55 of 55 families swept with a reason each (34 in, 21 out), EDGES_ONLY_COUNTS_PRINTED=0 -- the CTO's condition made falsifiable and held. TWO FINDINGS CHANGED THE NEXT ORDER BEFORE IT RAN, and G-2's face was amended @c4a842b1b9 and handed to the same slot: (a) SERVED_FROM (27 keys, derive_runner.py:1947-1955) lands on the same wrong class, so G2-AC2 now reads BOTH families -- repairing one and leaving the other is the per-member fix on a seam the census has shown is shared; (b) OWNED_BY already carries S3Key -> S3_BUCKET on 232 keys and ALL 135 STORED_IN sources carry one naming the same bucket, so a re-point mints a duplicate and a retirement loses nothing measurable. PITCHED (95002/95003), a VOCABULARY call and not mine under the W2-S45 precedent: RE-POINT or RETIRE STORED_IN. MY REC: RETIRE -- the estate spent round 6 paying for one fact carried in two places and a re-point would mint a third instance of that shape one round after the card wrote the lesson down; an absence is checked once, a duplicate has to agree forever. The order does NOT wait: default re-point, duplication filed as a row. THE CARD CAME BACK AS FOUR FILES (a carrier-SET card plus one row-card per carrier, because the contract's unit is one subject with seven rows and additionalProperties false), 21 of 21 rows with an owner and a distinguishable failure mode, and the shrink probe MASKED on the round's own 955 -> 137 and NOT on a fixed-emission pair with 6 of 6 controls. IT ALSO FOUND A DEFECT THE ROUND HAD NOT: the NODES carrier has NO drop-on-read (derive_stitch.py:437-455 drops an archived copy only when the same id is in this run's emission), so a node the producer STOPS emitting is served another cycle with no error and no count -- the nodes-carrier form of the sentence round 6 closed on, still open, owner 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp. Carried, not chased, and no running order widened with it. MY OWN CUT DEFECT, reported by the worker and owned here: G3-AC2 named .tools/validate-json-schema.py, which DOES NOT EXIST, and the v1 substrate-card schema, which the estate has superseded with v3.1 (const 1 vs const 3.1, mutually exclusive). The worker substituted the estate's real validator, passed 4 of 4 cards with 0 violations, and filed row W2-S73 instead of rescuing the criterion silently. Same class as F-5's .tools/comp-debt (S88): a SURFACES line written from the tool's NAME without a --name census. AND A CRITERION OF MINE WAS REFUTED, correctly: G3-AC5's premise that owner follows CARRIER is false -- owner follows the QUESTION (14 / 6 / 1 across 21 rows). Rule 24(iv) survives on the stronger case, one seat holding three remedies that measurably did not move together across four cycles. A judgment criterion exists to allow exactly that.
